key_cases.case_name: South Carolina Department of Social Services v. Meek
key_cases.court: Court of Appeals of South Carolina
key_cases.holding: The court reversed the portion of an order continuing DSS custody based on the mother's conduct, holding she was entitled to notice that DSS would seek custody at the father's merits hearing, while holding that omission of the statutory boldface notices from the removal petition did not divest the family court of subject matter jurisdiction.
key_cases.relevance: Meek turns on a Voluntary Placement Agreement and the process DSS owed the mother when she invoked it to request her children's return.
key_cases.quote: Mother's fundamental right to due process entitled her to notice that DSS intended to petition the family court for custody of the children at Father's hearing.

key_cases.case_name: Kaci May v. Dorchester School District Two
key_cases.citation: Op. No. 6053 (S.C. Ct. App. filed May 29, 2024) (App. Case No. 2020-001352)
key_cases.court: Court of Appeals of South Carolina
key_cases.holding: The court affirmed the denial of an injunction, holding S.C. Code § 63-7-920(C) authorizes DSS to interview children at school without a warrant and outside the parents' presence during a mandated investigation, and that the interviews here were reasonable in inception and scope under the Fourth Amendment.
key_cases.relevance: The investigation was triggered by the mother's own request for help, and the court holds she could not then dictate the terms of the resulting inquiry.
key_cases.quote: we find § 63-7-920(C) expressly authorizes DSS to interview children at school without a warrant when conducting an investigation mandated by § 63-7-920(A)(1)

key_cases.case_name: South Carolina Department of Social Services v. Mother
key_cases.court: Court of Appeals of South Carolina
key_cases.holding: The court reversed the portion of the family court's order directing DSS to forego reunification efforts and file a TPR petition, finding the preponderance of the evidence supported returning the twins home with twelve months of DSS supervision and services.
key_cases.relevance: The decision shows a parent who engaged with services successfully enough that continued in-home supervision, not removal, was the appropriate response.
key_cases.quote: we find the family court erred in ordering SCDSS to initiate TPR proceedings against Mother

mandatory_reporters: Listed professionals only, acting in their professional capacity (South Carolina is not a universal-reporter state) — S.C. Code Ann. § 63-7-310(A)
Physicians, nurses, dentists, optometrists, medical examiners, coroners, and employees of a county medical examiner's or coroner's office
Any other medical, emergency medical services, mental health, or allied health professional
Members of the clergy, including Christian Science practitioners and religious healers
Clerical or nonclerical religious counselors who charge for services
School teachers, counselors, principals, assistant principals, and school attendance officers
Childcare workers in a childcare center or foster care facility
Undertakers, funeral home directors, and employees of a funeral home
Volunteer non-attorney guardians ad litem serving on behalf of the South Carolina Guardian ad Litem Program or Richland County CASA
Any other person may report and is encouraged to report — S.C. Code Ann. § 63-7-310(D)

other: Encourages, condones, or approves the commission of delinquent acts by the child and those acts are shown to be the result of the encouragement, condonation, or approval
